name: PANAMA

flag.title: Flag of Panamá
flag.note: Four quarters: red, white, blue, white

lead: Panama is a skinny S-shaped country joining North and South America like a living bridge. Its famous Canal lets ships cut 13,000 km off their journey — giant locks lift vessels like bathtubs, shuffling 40 ships a day. Rainforests, coral reefs, and nearly 1,000 bird species make Panama one of the richest wild spots on Earth.

sections.animals: A jungle full of wild wonders

geo: Panama is so narrow you can stand on Volcán Barú and see both the Pacific and the Caribbean on a clear day — two oceans at once. Thick rainforest covers half the country, fed by over 3 m of rain a year.
The Canal cuts 80 km across the isthmus, linking two oceans and saving ships the long sail around South America. A watershed of lakes keeps the locks filled with freshwater all year round.
animals: Panama sits on a great migration highway. Billions of raptors — hawks, vultures, falcons — funnel through each autumn, filling the sky above Panama City. The harpy eagle, the Americas' most powerful bird of prey, still nests in remote jungle.

Sloths doze in trees along the Canal; jaguars prowl Darién; and the golden frog — Panama's national symbol — is now mostly kept in zoos to protect it from a deadly skin fungus that has swept the wild.
culture: Panamanians are proud of their mix: Spanish settlers, West African Canal workers, indigenous Guna people who sew vivid mola cloth, plus Chinese and Indian traders. That blend fills the food — patacones (fried plantain) sit beside ceviche and thick sancocho chicken soup.

Music pulses everywhere: salsa, reggaeton, and tamborito drums share the same dancefloor. At Carnival, elaborate pollera dresses — stitched by hand over months — twirl through Panama City streets each February in one of the Americas' biggest parties.
history: Indigenous peoples lived here thousands of years before the Spanish arrived in 1501. Panama City, founded 1519, became the Pacific's first European city and the exit point for gold looted from the Inca Empire across the mule trail Camino Real.

Panama broke from Colombia in 1903 — with US support — so the Canal could be built. The US ran the Canal Zone for nearly a century; Panama took full control on 31 December 1999, still celebrated as a national triumph.
wows: From Volcán Barú's summit you can see both the Pacific and the Caribbean Sea at the same time.
The Panama Canal earns around a third of Panama's entire government revenue from ship tolls.
More bird species live in Panama than in all of the USA and Canada put together.
The Guna people govern their own islands and decide who may visit or build there.
Panama uses US dollars but mints its own balboa coin at exactly 1-to-1 with the dollar.
Panama hats are actually made in Ecuador — Panama just shipped them to the world.
The 2016 Canal expansion lets ships carry 14,000 containers, ten times the 1914 capacity.

myths.fact: They are woven in Ecuador from toquilla straw — Panama just happened to be the trading hub that shipped them globally, so the name stuck.
Because of Panama's S-shape, ships travel roughly north–south — you exit into the Pacific slightly east of where you entered from the Caribbean.
